gates.title: Gate 1 — Are you in the Medi-Cal MAGI New Adult Group?
gates.body: First establish age, household size and coverage category. MAGI adult-expansion financial eligibility generally uses the 138% FPL limit; one-person 2026 references are $1,836/month and $22,025/year. Applicants are assessed on current monthly income under §435.603(h), not automatically annual income divided by 12. MAGI coverage has no asset test.
gates.if_yes: Go to Gate 2. DHCS targets Jan 1, 2027 for the work rule, subject to enacted implementation conditions; screen for exclusions and exemptions.
gates.if_no: If household MAGI is above the Medi-Cal adult-expansion limit, review Covered California. Marketplace help requires separate income, other-coverage and tax-filing eligibility; the 2026 single-person 400% FPL reference is $62,600. It is not guaranteed.

gates.title: Gate 2 — Can you show one qualifying month per renewal period?
gates.body: If you are in the MAGI New Adult Group and not excluded or exempt, you must demonstrate community engagement for at least one month between eligibility determinations (the months need not be consecutive). In that month you need one of: 80 hours of work (including in-kind or unpaid work), 80 hours of community service, 80 hours in a work program, at least half-time education, a combination totaling 80 hours, or monthly household income of at least $580 under MAGI-based financial methods.
gates.if_yes: Meeting a valid route satisfies this work-rule condition for the assessed period, provided all other Medi-Cal eligibility and renewal requirements are met.
gates.if_no: The county must send a notice and give you 30 calendar days to show compliance or an exemption. Coverage continues during the cure period. If you do not cure, you can be disenrolled and you are NOT eligible for federal premium tax credits while deemed Medicaid-eligible.

options.option: Medi-Cal — MAGI New Adult Group (aid code M1)
options.who: Adults 19–64, California residents, not pregnant, not on Medicare, household MAGI ≤ 138% FPL ($22,025/yr or $1,836/mo for one person in 2026). No asset test.
options.work_rule: DHCS target: January 1, 2027; enacted implementation conditions and exclusions apply. California uses one qualifying month per renewal period.
options.cost: $0 premium for most enrollees; cost sharing begins Oct 1, 2028 for some services.
options.how: Apply year-round at BenefitsCal or your county Medi-Cal office.

options.who: People 65+, blind, or disabled who meet the separate non-MAGI income and asset rules.
options.work_rule: No. The community engagement rule applies to the MAGI New Adult Group, not this group.
options.cost: Free or share-of-cost depending on income.
options.how: Apply through your county; disability determination may be required.

options.option: Covered California — with federal premium tax credit and/or state subsidy
options.who: U.S. citizens and lawfully present immigrants potentially eligible for marketplace financial help, subject to household MAGI, other coverage and filing rules. For 2026, the single-person 400% FPL reference is $62,600 (using 2025 FPL).
options.work_rule: No work requirement. Eligibility is income-based.
options.cost: 2026 federal applicable percentage: 2.10% to 9.96% of household income for the benchmark Silver plan. California adds a state subsidy at or below 165% FPL in 2026 and 200% FPL in 2027.
options.how: Apply at CoveredCA.com during open enrollment (Nov 1–Jan 31) or a special enrollment period.

options.option: Covered California — full price, no subsidy
options.who: Household income above 400% FPL, or otherwise ineligible for financial help.
options.cost: Full premium. No official statewide average premium is published for your profile, so this site leaves the dollar figure blank and flags it.
options.how: Apply at CoveredCA.com; compare plans by region and metal tier.

options.who: Medicare eligibility must be established separately; this user’s age, disability and entitlement are unknown.
options.work_rule: No. Medicare Part A or B enrollment is a mandatory exception to the Medicaid work rule.
options.cost: Personal premium and cost-sharing amounts are not established.
options.how: Review Medicare eligibility with Social Security; no enrollment determination made here.

options.who: Anyone, regardless of insurance or income. This is access to care, not comprehensive insurance.
options.cost: Sliding fee based on income; HRSA requires a full discount at or below 100% FPL, with possible nominal charges.
options.how: Find a HRSA-funded health center and ask for the sliding-fee program.

pathways.what: At least 80 hours per month of work. The federal rule defines work to include work in exchange for goods or services (“in-kind” work) and expressly says a property manager or building superintendent who receives free or reduced rent can count the hours spent on those duties.
pathways.fit: Potential fit only for documented property-management duties exchanged for free or reduced rent, as in the CMS example. An owner’s routine rental ownership is not automatically this route.
pathways.note: The federal rule is explicit. The county's documentation process for in-kind work is not yet published; keep a duty list, rent-credit agreement, and monthly hours log. No cash wages does not establish zero taxable compensation; the tax treatment of housing is a separate question.

pathways.what: DHCS lists self-employment work among ways to reach 80 hours in a month. Whether an owner’s management of their own rental property meets that work definition depends on actual duties and county verification; the tax passive-activity label alone does not decide it.
pathways.fit: Possible if actual, documented management work reaches 80 hours and the county confirms it qualifies; not automatic for ownership alone.
pathways.note: Ask the county how owner-management hours are counted and what documentation is accepted; do not claim eligibility from a lease or an IRS schedule alone.

pathways.what: Monthly income of at least $580, determined using MAGI-based financial methods for the individual’s MAGI-based household budget. DHCS’s earlier letter says “income from any source” and “before taxes”; those phrases do not make gross rent, trading payouts or deposits automatically countable.
pathways.fit: Potentially useful without wages if properly determined countable household income reaches $580 in a qualifying month. Exact rent, interest and Kalshi tax amounts are unknown.
pathways.note: Enacted California law and CMS require MAGI-based methods. The household and tax classification are unknown; no personal pass is established.

pathways.path: Six-month income average for seasonal workers
pathways.what: A seasonal worker under IRC §45R(d)(5)(B) may meet the income alternative with an average of at least $580/month over the preceding six months, using the MAGI-based household budget. Earlier preliminary DHCS material uses broader fluctuating-hours language, but the enacted California statute requires seasonal-worker status.
pathways.fit: Only if the applicant is a qualifying seasonal worker; lumpy Kalshi or rental income alone does not establish this route.
pathways.note: Seasonal-worker status for this person has not been established. Use the one-month method or another qualifying activity instead of assuming blanket averaging.

pathways.what: At least 80 hours per month of unpaid work with a structured program that benefits the community, under a public or nonprofit organization that tracks hours and can confirm them through a named contact. It cannot serve a partisan purpose.
pathways.fit: Fallback if the work and income routes do not fit.
pathways.note: Keep a signed hour log and the organization's contact information.

pathways.what: At least 80 hours per month in a work program as defined in section 6(o)(1) of the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008, including certain state employment and training programs and veterans' training programs.
pathways.note: Ask the county which local programs qualify before enrolling.

pathways.what: Enrollment in an educational program at least half-time. The school or institution determines full-time, half-time, or less-than-half-time status. Less-than-half-time credit hours can be converted to hours (credit hours × 3 × 4.33) and combined with other activities.
pathways.note: The site does not assume a fixed “6 credits” definition; the institution's determination controls.

pathways.what: Any combination of work, community service, work program, and less-than-half-time education totaling at least 80 hours in the month.
pathways.fit: Useful if no single activity reaches 80 hours.
pathways.note: Hours must be documented activity by activity.

pathways.path: Exclusion, mandatory exception, or short-term hardship
pathways.what: Certain people are excluded from the rule or deemed compliant: former foster youth under 26, American Indians/Alaska Natives, parents/caretakers of a child 13 or younger or a disabled person, veterans with a total disability rating, medically frail people, TANF/SNAP work-requirement compliance, SUD treatment participants, inmates, pregnant/postpartum people, people under 19, people on Medicare, and people in a high-unemployment or disaster county. Inpatient care and medical travel can be short-term hardships if requested.
pathways.fit: Depends on personal facts not supplied. Ask the county to screen for every exclusion first.
pathways.note: Screen the distinct exclusion and hardship criteria. The June 29 lawsuit filing is verified; present court disposition is not.

findings.finding: Qualifying activities
findings.value: 80 hours of work, community service, work program or combined activities; OR at least half-time education
findings.detail: Half-time enrollment independently satisfies the condition: it does not also require 80 hours. Less-than-half-time education can be combined with other qualifying activities.

findings.finding: Income alternative
findings.detail: A monthly income not less than the federal minimum wage multiplied by 80 hours. The federal minimum wage is $7.25 in 2026, so the threshold is $580.

review.locator: CMS CIB §V(F)

findings.finding: Seasonal-worker alternative
findings.value: Average of at least $580 per month over the preceding 6 months
findings.detail: The statute limits this alternative to a seasonal worker as described in IRC §45R(d)(5)(B).

findings.finding: Verification and cure
findings.value: Reliable information first; 30-day notice; coverage continues
findings.detail: AB 2161 §14005.69(j)–(n): reliable information first, then notice and 30 calendar days beginning with receipt. Existing members keep coverage during that period; other eligibility bases and hearing rights must be considered before denial/disenrollment.

findings.finding: Renewal standard
findings.value: One or more months between determinations; months need not be consecutive
findings.detail: CMS interprets the statute to mean a beneficiary is compliant if they demonstrated community engagement for the number of months the state specifies during any part of the eligibility period.

findings.finding: Consequence of noncompliance
findings.value: Denial or disenrollment after cure; no federal premium tax credit while deemed Medicaid-eligible
findings.detail: CMS CIB §VII: a person otherwise eligible for Medicaid but for failure to demonstrate community engagement is deemed eligible for minimum essential coverage for APTC/PTC purposes. This is not a lifetime ban on marketplace aid.

ca_actions.action: Implements the federal work rule for the MAGI New Adult Group (M1)
ca_actions.detail: DHCS publishes January 1, 2027 as its target. AB 2161 requires no earlier than that date, systems readiness and applicable federal approvals; funding-related deferral provisions also exist.

ca_actions.action: Moves M1 adults to six-month renewals
ca_actions.detail: The policy is effective January 1, 2027; DHCS says the first impacted members are expected to have renewal dates beginning March 1, 2027.

DHCS began texting members in February 2026, mailed outreach notices in late August 2026, and requires the outreach letter with application materials from October 1 through December 31, 2026. Materials are translated into all threshold languages.

ca_actions.action: Requires counties to check existing data first
ca_actions.detail: Counties must attempt ex parte verification using reliable information before asking the member for documents. If verification fails, the member gets a notice and 30 calendar days to cure while coverage continues.

ca_actions.action: Applies the federal exclusions and exceptions, including county-wide hardship
ca_actions.detail: California's exemption table includes high-unemployment counties (lesser of 8% or 1.5 times the national rate), federally declared disaster counties, Medicare, pregnancy/postpartum, parents of a child 13 or younger, medically frail people, and others.

The enacted 2026-27 budget reflects about $1.3B General Fund in H.R.1-related Medi-Cal costs and $196.8M General Fund for county eligibility workload. DHCS projects $357.6M in work-rule savings in 2026-27 and 43,000 work-rule disenrollments, rising to 1.1 million by 2029-30.

California co-leads Commonwealth of Massachusetts et al. v. Mehmet Oz with Massachusetts and New Jersey; the coalition is 24 attorneys general plus the governors of Kentucky and Pennsylvania. The suit challenges the IFR's narrowing of the medically-frail protection. Filed June 29, 2026.

ca_actions.action: Funds a state premium subsidy for Covered California
ca_actions.detail: 2026: $190 million appropriated, subsidy available up to 165% FPL (S18). 2027: $300 million, up to 200% FPL ($31,920 for an individual, $66,000 for a family of four). Covered California projects more than 500,000 enrollees receive it in 2027.

ca_actions.action: Does not provide a blanket exemption for zero-earned-income adults
ca_actions.detail: No such exemption appears in ACWDL 25-30 or the Medi-Cal Changes page. The state routes are the federal work, income, education, community-service and exemption routes described on this site.

ca_actions.action: Counts in-kind work and income from any source
ca_actions.detail: The rule counts in-kind work, including the published rent-credit property-manager example. The income alternative uses MAGI-based household methods, not gross deposits. Neither route is established for this user without the missing facts.

flags.item: Personal eligibility facts are missing
flags.issue: Age, household size, county, exact income amounts, tax filing status, pregnancy/disability status, and current coverage were not supplied. Every personal eligibility determination is therefore left blank.
flags.impact: The site can explain the rules but cannot say whether you qualify. The county must decide.

flags.item: Kalshi federal tax classification is unresolved
flags.issue: No IRS revenue ruling, regulation, notice, or FAQ specific to Kalshi-type event contracts was located. Capital, ordinary, section 1256, and gambling treatments remain possible.
flags.impact: The classification changes MAGI, loss netting, and the 90% gambling-loss cap.

flags.item: Tax form for Kalshi event-contract trading is not verified
flags.issue: An official federal source describing what 1099, if any, Kalshi issues for event-contract results was not established. General IRS recordkeeping guidance does not specify this platform’s forms.
flags.impact: Keep complete transactions, basis and proceeds records; obtain qualified tax advice without assuming a missing 1099 means no tax duty.

flags.item: Section 1256 applicability is uncertain
flags.issue: Kalshi is a CFTC DCM, but its event contracts are described as swaps. Whether they are regulated futures contracts under IRC §1256 has not been ruled on.
flags.impact: Section 1256 would impose 60/40 treatment and year-end mark-to-market, including phantom income on open positions.

flags.item: Gambling treatment and the 90% loss cap
flags.issue: If Kalshi gains were treated as gambling, losses would be itemized deductions only up to winnings, and H.R.1 §70114 caps the deduction at 90% of losses for tax years after 2025.
flags.impact: A break-even trader could owe tax on income they did not keep.

flags.item: H.R. 10357 is not law
flags.issue: The Digital Asset Tax Certainty Act's Title VII (§701) would rewrite IRC §165(d) so wagering losses are allowed only to the extent of wagering gains — repealing the 90% cap in H.R.1 §70114. The Ways and Means Committee approved a substitute 38–5 on September 16, 2026, but the bill has not passed the House or Senate.
flags.impact: The 90% cap remains current law for 2026 unless the bill is enacted.

flags.item: Preliminary gross-income wording versus enacted MAGI method
flags.issue: ACWDL 25-30 says “total gross income,” but later-enacted AB 2161 §14005.69(e)(6) requires MAGI-based financial methods for the individual’s household budget. The actual rent/expenses and tax reporting are unknown.
flags.impact: Use the enacted MAGI-based method, not gross rent receipts or bank deposits. Ask the county to apply the later statute to the documented household income.

flags.item: Household composition for the $580 income alternative is unknown
flags.issue: Enacted AB 2161 §14005.69(e)(6) refers to the individual’s MAGI-based household budget. The outreach letter’s “your income” wording does not establish a single-person household.
flags.impact: The household and tax-filing facts were not supplied. Ask the county how income from household members is counted.

flags.item: Seasonal-worker status is not established for this applicant
flags.issue: Federal law and enacted AB 2161 §14005.69(e)(7) require a seasonal worker for the six-month average. Earlier preliminary DHCS material mentioned variable hours, but lumpy Kalshi trading by itself is not proof of seasonal work.
flags.impact: Do not average six trading months as an automatic fallback; establish seasonal-worker status or use another route.

flags.item: DHCS says the rules start January 1, 2027, but its member letter says March 2027
flags.issue: The MEDIL I26-25 member letter says “these rules will not go into effect until March 2027.” DHCS's public pages say the work rules start January 1, 2027 and six-month renewals start March 1, 2027.
flags.impact: Ask DHCS/county to reconcile the dates; do not infer a cause for the discrepancy or postpone records on that basis.

flags.item: Six-month renewal date has been stated inconsistently
flags.issue: DHCS distinguishes the January 2027 policy date and March 2027 first affected renewal dates. This distinction does not establish the renewal date of this user.
flags.impact: New applicants may be subject to the six-month cycle earlier than existing members. Follow the county notice.

flags.item: DHCS's public page describes the income test as work earnings
flags.issue: The Medi-Cal Changes page says “work at a job and earn at least $580 a month,” while MEDIL I26-25 says “income from any source.”
flags.impact: The public page is narrower than the official guidance. The site relies on the official guidance and flags the discrepancy.

flags.item: State count differs across official sources
flags.issue: CMS says 43 states and DC provide coverage to these populations. CRS says 40 states and DC adopted the ACA expansion as of August 2025. The data file previously said 41 expansion states plus DC plus waiver states.
flags.impact: No effect on California eligibility; the figures measure different things and dates.

flags.item: High-unemployment wording differs
flags.issue: The statute and CMS CIB say the lesser of 8% or 1.5 times the national rate. The CMS fact sheet phrases it as “8% or 1.5 times.”
flags.impact: Use the statutory lesser-of standard. The county determines whether your county qualifies.

flags.item: Full-price Covered California premiums are not published as a single official figure
flags.issue: Personal age, rating area, household, plan and coverage details were not supplied. A general average cannot establish this person’s premium.
flags.impact: The site leaves the dollar amount blank rather than estimating.

flags.item: The 60–70% procedural-loss figure is not verified
flags.issue: The prior site presented “60–70% of projected national coverage losses are procedural” without an official source. This site does not use that figure. DHCS does say procedural and paperwork discontinuances are expected to rise.
flags.impact: Treat any specific percentage as a projection or third-party estimate, not an official fact.

flags.item: In-kind work documentation process is not yet published
flags.issue: The federal rule explicitly counts a property manager's in-kind work, but DHCS has not published a specific form or verification standard for in-kind hours.
flags.impact: Keep a contemporaneous duty list, rent-credit agreement and monthly hours log; ask the county what it will accept.

flags.item: Owner-management hours are not explicitly addressed
flags.issue: The IFR example is a property manager who receives free or reduced rent. Whether an owner who manages their own rental property can count those hours as self-employment is not spelled out in DHCS guidance.
flags.impact: An owner’s actual activities and documentation require review. No approval of owner-management or personal trading hours is assumed.

flags.item: The medically-frail definition is being litigated
flags.issue: The IFR narrows “medically frail” to people whose condition significantly impairs their ability to comply. California and other states are challenging that narrowing.
flags.impact: The June 29 filing is established; no current docket outcome or injunction was verified. Do not assume the filing suspends the rule.

flags.item: Aged and Disabled asset limits change on July 1, 2027
flags.issue: The non-MAGI asset limit drops from $130,000 to $21,000 for one person on July 1, 2027.
flags.impact: This does not affect MAGI Medi-Cal, but it matters if you qualify through age or disability.

flags.item: Failing the work rule also blocks premium tax credits
flags.issue: A person who does not comply is deemed Medicaid-eligible and is not eligible for federal subsidies to buy marketplace coverage.
flags.impact: The fallback is not automatically Covered California with subsidies. You must cure, reapply, or qualify for Medicaid again.

flags.item: The site's earlier $1.1B characterization was inaccurate
flags.issue: The earlier site said $1.1B was appropriated “to implement” the work rule and “to minimize procedural coverage loss.” That is not what the documents say. In the January 2026 budget, $1.1B is the projected MCO-tax transition cost and, separately, the ongoing cost of full-scope coverage for affected immigrants. The enacted 2026-27 Budget Act reflects about $1.3B General Fund in H.R.1-related Medi-Cal costs.
flags.impact: The misattribution is removed. The enacted figure now carries the enacted source.

flags.item: The site's earlier “lead plaintiff” wording was imprecise
flags.issue: California co-leads the coalition with Massachusetts and New Jersey. The case caption names Massachusetts first.
flags.impact: Co-lead wording and June 29 date corrected in primary and California detail data/pages.

flags.item: The site's earlier $1,835 monthly figure was off by $1
flags.issue: DHCS publishes $1,836/month at 138% FPL for a one-person household in 2026.
flags.impact: Corrected on the primary pages.

flags.item: Earlier core used a 2027 marketplace FPL figure for 2026 coverage
flags.issue: The 2026 Covered California Open Enrollment Highlights explicitly places 400% FPL at $62,600 for one individual in plan year 2026. The $63,840 reference belongs to 2027 marketplace coverage.
flags.impact: The primary dashboard, findings and coverage bands now separate the two plan years.

flags.item: 2027 Medi-Cal income limit for this household
flags.issue: A 2026 DHCS Medi-Cal chart and a 2027 marketplace FPL chart do not determine the 2027 Medi-Cal limit. The applicant’s household size is unknown.
flags.impact: The future Medi-Cal dollar amount is blank, not copied from a different year or program.

flags.item: Earlier third-party California coverage-loss forecasts not reverified
flags.issue: Older detail pages quoted CHCF, urban-model and news figures with no directly linked official underlying model. Only DHCS’s own enacted-budget projections are carried as published values here; other figures remain blank.
flags.impact: Statewide model outputs are not this person’s coverage outcome. Compare DHCS work-rule and all-H.R.1 projections separately.

flags.item: Present lawsuit disposition not established
flags.issue: The June 29 Attorney General release proves filing, not the current docket status.
flags.impact: No injunction or suspension of the rule is assumed.

flags.item: Budget PDF omits a unit
flags.issue: DHCS budget text says “$90.3 General Fund” beside the $357.6 million work-rule reduction without a unit for the parenthetical component.
flags.impact: The primary finding omits that component rather than silently adding “million”.

flags.item: 2027 marketplace dollar-column extraction gap
flags.issue: The retrieved official 2027 FPL chart establishes the percentage ceiling, but its text extraction omitted the final dollar column.
flags.impact: Current primary pages leave that dollar amount blank; earlier archived $63,840 figures were not freshly certified.

flags.item: Historical audit falsely reported an age discrepancy
flags.issue: “Under 14” and “13 years of age and under” mean the same age boundary.
flags.impact: Corrected in the current findings; the dated independent audit is preserved as historical material.

flags.item: Personal owner-management and trading hours unknown
flags.issue: No official source confirms the accepted hours for this user.
flags.impact: Do not certify either activity from a job title or a tax classification.

flags.item: Actual DHCS caregiver-age wording discrepancy
flags.issue: The DHCS Tracking Federal Impact page says adults without children “under 13”; the codified rule and AB 2161 use age 13 or younger. These are different boundaries.
flags.impact: Use the enacted/codified age boundary and obtain county review; do not confuse this with the equivalent phrases “under 14” and “13 or younger”.

flags.item: California describes the income test three different ways
flags.issue: DHCS's public page says “work at a job and earn at least $580 a month”; its member letter says “income from any source”; the enacted statute and the regulation require MAGI-based household income.
flags.impact: A reader could wrongly conclude that only wages count, or that every deposit counts. Neither is the rule: net rent, interest and recognized gains count; gross receipts and returned deposits do not.

flags.item: California's averaging guidance is broader than the federal rule
flags.issue: ACWDL 25-30 offers six-month averaging to anyone whose income fluctuates. 42 CFR 435.552(g) limits averaging to a seasonal worker described in IRC §45R(d)(5)(B). DHCS's public page now says “seasonal worker,” matching the regulation.
flags.impact: If you are not a statutory seasonal worker, do not rely on averaging. Use one qualifying month measured on its own.

flags.item: California implementation approval and operative details need confirmation
flags.issue: The reviewed sources do not establish the final approved state-plan status. AB2161 sets the previous-month application and any-one-month renewal rules, subject to its express implementation conditions; federal discretion alone does not erase the enacted state law.
flags.impact: Follow the enacted California rule and the actual notice, while checking later DHCS implementation instructions.

flags.item: No published California standard for documenting owner-management hours
flags.issue: The reviewed general sources do not establish acceptance or a complete documentation standard for this person’s owner-management hours.
flags.impact: Ask the county which activities and evidence it accepts. A log is useful suggested evidence, not a guaranteed or exclusive safeguard.

flags.item: In-kind rent may be income as well as hours
flags.issue: IRS Topic 420 gives a general fair-market-value inclusion rule for barter. Whether a particular lodging arrangement is taxable or excluded and how it enters monthly MAGI still requires its facts.
flags.impact: Do not count housing twice or invent its value. Obtain advice on tax treatment and county income allocation before relying on it.

action_plan.action: Identify the correct household and countable income
action_plan.detail: Age, household size, county and income amounts were not supplied. Start with the household rules and separate current monthly Medi-Cal MAGI from annual marketplace income. Net rent and interest can count without wages. Do not assume a one-person household.

action_plan.action: If MAGI is at or below 138% FPL, apply for or keep Medi-Cal
action_plan.detail: Apply year-round at BenefitsCal or through your county. There is no asset test for MAGI Medi-Cal.

action_plan.action: Document your property-management work every month
action_plan.detail: If there is a real in-kind property-management arrangement, retain duty records, the housing/rent-credit agreement and dated hour records. CMS expressly recognizes this type of work. Owning rental property or describing yourself as a manager does not establish qualifying hours.

Keep records of countable household MAGI-based income, including allowable rental expenses and supported tax treatment. At least $580 in an assessed month can satisfy the rule; savings withdrawals and gross trading payouts are not automatically income.

action_plan.action: Respond promptly to notices; preserve hearing rights
action_plan.detail: AB 2161 provides a 30-calendar-day period beginning with receipt and deems receipt five days after the notice date. Existing-member coverage continues as specified. Follow the actual notice and appeal deadline; do not assume an extra month to create missing historical hours.

action_plan.action: If MAGI is above 138% FPL, go to Covered California
action_plan.detail: There is no work requirement. Check the federal premium tax credit and the California state subsidy. If you are above 400% FPL, the federal credit is unavailable for 2026.

action_plan.action: Get the Kalshi tax classification reviewed before you file
action_plan.detail: Federal classification affects household MAGI and loss treatment. Keep complete event-contract transaction, basis and proceeds records; an official source has not established which 1099 form (if any) Kalshi issues for those results.

routes.route: 80 hours of work in the month
routes.must: At least 80 hours of work — including in-kind work and unpaid work — in the month being reviewed. Qualifying unpaid work is not all unpaid activity: owner-management and personal trading hours are not automatically accepted.
routes.collect: Duty list; free or reduced-rent agreement; monthly hours log; leases or management agreement; owner or witness statement.

routes.route: $580 of MAGI-based household income in the month
routes.must: Monthly MAGI-based household income of at least $580 (the federal minimum wage, $7.25, times 80 hours).
routes.collect: Schedule E or rent ledger with expenses; 1099-INT; Kalshi statement and P&L; prior return as a cross-check.

routes.route: Community service, a work program, or school
routes.must: 80 hours of community service or a work program in the month; at least half-time enrollment; or a combination totaling 80 hours. Education hours combine only when enrollment is less than half-time.
routes.collect: Program timesheet or supervisor letter; school enrollment verification (the school decides half-time status).

routes.must: A listed status — for example a parent or caretaker of a child 13 or younger or of a disabled person, Medicare, medically frail, a recent inmate, or a state-option hardship.
routes.collect: Evidence of the specific status the county names (Medicare card, birth certificate, care plan, discharge papers).

income_types.how: Schedule E: rents minus mortgage interest, property tax, insurance, repairs, depreciation and other allowable expenses.
MAGI uses net rental income, not the rent check. Using gross rent overstates countable income and can push a household over 138% FPL.
Reported on 1099-INT and 1099-DIV; already inside AGI.
Added back to AGI when computing MAGI even though it is not federally taxed.

income_types.type: Free or reduced rent received for management work
income_types.counts: Generally taxable if it is barter; individual treatment unresolved
income_types.how: Topic 420 gives a general fair-market-value rule; exclusions, employee arrangements, personal valuation and monthly treatment require review. No ownership-only tax conclusion is inferred.

income_types.counts: Yes, if recognized and in AGI
income_types.how: Amount depends on classification (capital, ordinary, section 1256, or gambling). Character unresolved — see F40 and F42.

income_types.counts: Nonprofessional Schedule A losses do not reduce AGI
income_types.how: Conditional on nonprofessional gambling treatment. Enacted §70114 applies the 90%-of-losses rule from 2026, capped at gains; Topic 419 alone omits that update. Personal/professional treatment remains unresolved.
The Marketplace income rules list gifts and loan proceeds as income that is not counted.

evidence.proves: Dates, duties and hours for each qualifying month
evidence.why: A contemporaneous log is suggested evidence of which month work occurred; it is not the only permissible record or proof of accepted activity.

evidence.doc: Free or reduced-rent agreement, or lease addendum
evidence.proves: That management duties are exchanged for housing (in-kind work)
evidence.why: CMS's own example is a property manager or building superintendent receiving free or reduced rent.

evidence.doc: Duty list, management agreement, vendor invoices
evidence.proves: The duties actually performed and who performed them
evidence.why: Ownership of a building is not evidence of hours; the county needs the duties.

evidence.doc: Schedule E or rent ledger with expenses
evidence.proves: Net rental income for the month
evidence.why: MAGI counts net rent, so every expense claimed should be documented.
Interest is MAGI even when it is small or tax-exempt.

evidence.doc: Kalshi account statement and profit-and-loss report
evidence.proves: Realized gains and losses by month
evidence.why: The IRS recordkeeping rules require records that substantiate reported income; the platform statement is the starting point.

evidence.doc: Notices from the county or DHCS
evidence.proves: The action, the reason, and the cure deadline
evidence.why: AB2161 gives 30 calendar days from receipt, with receipt presumed five calendar days after the notice date. Preserve the envelope and actual receipt evidence.

calendar.what: Pick the month you will rely on and assemble its evidence.
calendar.do: At application, California reviews the month immediately before the month of application.

calendar.what: Make sure Medi-Cal has your current address, phone and email.
calendar.do: DHCS says it will send letters; a missed letter can become a missed cure deadline.

calendar.what: The work rule is scheduled to start in California.
calendar.do: Open any county letter and respond; ask first whether an exclusion or exception applies.

calendar.what: 30 calendar days from receipt under AB2161; receipt presumed five days after notice date.
calendar.do: Respond in writing, attach the log, and keep proof of submission. Coverage continues during the cure period.

calendar.what: DHCS published start for more frequent eligibility checks; not everyone’s individual renewal date.
calendar.do: AB2161 uses any one qualifying month since the latest determination at renewal. Follow the actual notice and implementation conditions.

calendar.what: Non-MAGI asset limits fall to $21,000 for one person.
calendar.do: Relevant only if you leave the MAGI group — for example at Medicare age.

calendar.what: Copays begin for some adults above 100% FPL.
calendar.do: Up to $35 per service, capped at 5% of household income; preventive and emergency care are excluded.
